```{r setup, include=FALSE}
source("../../_shared/template/viscount_rmd_helpers.R")

sett_raw <- jsonlite::fromJSON("postcolonial_east_africa_settlements.json", simplifyVector = FALSE)
summary_cache <- jsonlite::fromJSON("postcolonial_east_africa_summary_cache.json", simplifyVector = FALSE)

all_keys <- names(sett_raw)
all_entries <- lapply(all_keys, function (k) {
  e <- sett_raw[[k]]
  e$key <- k
  e
})

iso3_map <- c(
  "Burundi" = "BDI",
  "Democratic Republic of the Congo" = "COD",
  "Ethiopia" = "ETH",
  "Kenya" = "KEN",
  "Malawi" = "MWI",
  "Mozambique" = "MOZ",
  "Rwanda" = "RWA",
  "Somalia" = "SOM",
  "South Sudan" = "SSD",
  "Uganda" = "UGA",
  "United Republic of Tanzania" = "TZA",
  "Zambia" = "ZMB"
)

fmt_eu_coord <- function (x) {
  s <- format(round(as.numeric(x), 2L), nsmall = 2L, trim = TRUE)
  gsub("\\.", ",", s)
}

interp_site_pop <- function (e, yr_num) {
  ps <- e$population
  if (is.null(ps) || length(ps) == 0L) return(NA_real_)
  yrs <- as.numeric(names(ps))
  vals <- as.numeric(unlist(ps))
  ord <- order(yrs)
  yrs <- yrs[ord]
  vals <- vals[ord]
  if (yr_num < yrs[1] || yr_num > yrs[length(yrs)]) return(NA_real_)
  idx <- which(yrs == yr_num)
  if (length(idx) > 0L) return(vals[idx[1]])
  stats::approx(x = yrs, y = vals, xout = yr_num, method = "linear")$y
}

fmt_site_pop <- function (e, yr_num) {
  p <- interp_site_pop(e, yr_num)
  if (is.na(p) || p <= 0) return("-")
  viscount_fmt_pop(p)
}

fmt_site_peak <- function (e) {
  ps <- e$population
  if (is.null(ps) || length(ps) == 0L) return("-")
  yrs <- as.numeric(names(ps))
  vals <- as.numeric(unlist(ps))
  i_pk <- which.max(vals)
  paste0(viscount_fmt_pop(vals[i_pk]), " (", yrs[i_pk], "AD)")
}

entry_peak <- function (e) {
  ps <- e$population
  if (is.null(ps) || length(ps) == 0L) return(0)
  max(as.numeric(unlist(ps)))
}

sort_entries_desc <- function (sub_list) {
  pks <- vapply(sub_list, entry_peak, numeric(1))
  nms <- vapply(sub_list, function (e) as.character(e$name), character(1))
  sub_list[order(-pks, nms)]
}

core_countries <- c(
  "Kenya",
  "United Republic of Tanzania",
  "Uganda",
  "Rwanda",
  "Burundi",
  "Democratic Republic of the Congo"
)

border_countries <- c("Malawi", "Zambia", "South Sudan", "Somalia", "Ethiopia", "Mozambique")
all_country_order <- c(core_countries, border_countries)

entries_by_country <- setNames(lapply(all_country_order, function (cn) {
  sub <- Filter(function (e) identical(as.character(e$country), cn), all_entries)
  sort_entries_desc(sub)
}), all_country_order)

border_entries <- sort_entries_desc(
  Filter(function (e) as.character(e$country) %in% border_countries, all_entries)
)

build_gazetteer_df <- function (sub_list) {
  rows <- lapply(sub_list, function (e) {
    iso_code <- iso3_map[[as.character(e$country)]]
    if (is.null(iso_code)) iso_code <- toupper(substr(as.character(e$country), 1L, 3L))
    loc_str <- paste0(iso_code, ": ", fmt_eu_coord(e$coords[[1]]), ", ", fmt_eu_coord(e$coords[[2]]))
    sc_str <- if (identical(e$population_scope, "metro")) "Metro" else "City"
    data.frame(
      Settlement = as.character(e$name),
      Scope = sc_str,
      Location = loc_str,
      `1961AD` = fmt_site_pop(e, 1961),
      `1981AD` = fmt_site_pop(e, 1981),
      `2000AD` = fmt_site_pop(e, 2000),
      `2025AD` = fmt_site_pop(e, 2025),
      Peak = fmt_site_peak(e),
      check.names = FALSE,
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    )
  })
  df <- do.call(rbind, rows)
  rownames(df) <- NULL
  df
}

n_excluded <- as.integer(summary_cache$wave_saturation_stats$ledger_excluded)
n_candidates <- length(all_entries) + n_excluded
bench_nums <- c(1961, 1976, 1991, 2000, 2015, 2025)
bench_keys <- as.character(bench_nums)
n_active <- setNames(
  vapply(bench_nums, function (yr) sum(vapply(all_entries, function (e) !is.na(interp_site_pop(e, yr)), logical(1))), integer(1)),
  bench_keys
)
```

# Abstract

This gazetteer compiles coordinates, spatial scope classifications and multi-decade population series for `r viscount_fmt_number(length(all_entries), 0L)` assessed towns and metropolitan agglomerations across twelve East and Central African countries between 1961AD and 2025AD. Screened from `r viscount_fmt_number(n_candidates, 0L)` candidate municipal and urban entries (`r viscount_fmt_number(n_excluded, 0L)` duplicate aliases excluded), the retained ledger spans `r viscount_fmt_number(summary_cache$observation_count, 0L)` dated observations across `r viscount_fmt_number(summary_cache$population_scope_counts$city_proper, 0L)` city-proper units and `r viscount_fmt_number(summary_cache$population_scope_counts$metro, 0L)` metropolitan agglomerations. Active interpolated entries rise from `r viscount_fmt_number(n_active[["1961"]], 0L)` towns in 1961AD to `r viscount_fmt_number(n_active[["1991"]], 0L)` in 1991AD, `r viscount_fmt_number(n_active[["2000"]], 0L)` in 2000AD, `r viscount_fmt_number(n_active[["2015"]], 0L)` in 2015AD and `r viscount_fmt_number(n_active[["2025"]], 0L)` in 2025AD, documenting urban hierarchies from primate national capitals such as Nairobi, Dar es Salaam, Kampala, Kigali and Bujumbura down to rural market towns across Uganda, Kenya, Tanzania, Rwanda, Burundi and adjacent border corridors.

```{r fig1-md-only, results='asis'}
if (!knitr::is_latex_output()) {
  viscount_figure(
    "figures/fig_01_map.png",
    "Spatial distribution of 1.880 assessed towns and agglomerations across Uganda, Kenya, Tanzania, Rwanda, Burundi and border zones from 1961AD to 2025AD.",
    "fig:hero-settlements-east-africa"
  )
}
```

# Background

Reconstructing urban settlement hierarchies in post-colonial East Africa requires harmonising statutory municipal census divisions with satellite-detected built-up footprints [@KNBS2019KenyaCensus; @NBSTanzania2022Census; @UBOS2024UgandaCensus; @OECD2024Africapolis]. Whereas administrative city limits in Nairobi, Dar es Salaam, Kampala, Kigali and Bujumbura capture core municipal districts, rapid peri-urban expansion after 1990AD pushed urban populations far beyond colonial town boundaries into surrounding counties and highland corridors [@Bank2012EastAfrican; @Bank2017RwandaEconomic; @Hayashi2007LongTerm]. Compiling both city-proper census series and metropolitan agglomerations within a single ledger preserves comparability across all twelve jurisdictions inside the East African study rectangle [@Tatem2007HighResolution; @Runfola2020GeoBoundaries].

# Methodology

## Candidate Screening and Territorial Scope

Candidate urban records were screened from KNBS, NBS/OCGS, UBOS, NISR and ISTEEBU census volumes, UNSD Demographic Yearbook tables and Africapolis [@KNBS2019KenyaCensus; @NBSTanzania2022Census; @UBOS2024UgandaCensus; @OECD2024Africapolis]. Of `r viscount_fmt_number(n_candidates, 0L)` candidates within the `r viscount_fmt_number(summary_cache$total_area_km2, 0L)` km² study frame, `r viscount_fmt_number(n_excluded, 0L)` overlapping synonym records were merged or excluded, retaining `r viscount_fmt_number(length(all_entries), 0L)` assessed settlements across `r viscount_fmt_number(summary_cache$observation_count, 0L)` observations. Five core republics account for 1.735 entries - Tanzania (522), Uganda (519), Kenya (418), Burundi (198) and Rwanda (78) - alongside 145 adjacent border-zone towns in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo (112), Malawi (10), Zambia (6), South Sudan (6), Somalia (4), Ethiopia (4) and Mozambique (3).

## Interpolation and Scope Conventions

Each entry reports either municipal city-proper populations (*City*) or continuous morphological agglomerations (*Metro*). Regional tables present linearly interpolated populations at four benchmark dates (1961AD, 1981AD, 2000AD and 2025AD) alongside each entry's peak population and peak year; benchmarks outside a town's observed span are marked with a hyphen (-). Notice that in densely farmed Lake Victoria, Mount Kenya, Mount Elgon and northern Burundi corridors, Africapolis morphological clusters merge extensive rural-urban settlements into multi-million conurbations (such as Kisumu, Embu, Mbale and Kayanza) that far exceed statutory town boundaries [@OECD2024Africapolis].

# Testing and Validation

Rank-size regression across the upper 180 urban peaks yields $q = 1,06$ ($R^2 = 0,99$), while full-sample regression across all `r viscount_fmt_number(length(all_entries), 0L)` entries yields $q = 1,14$ ($R^2 = 0,95$), aligning closely with the 1.764 spatially deduplicated centres plotted in Figure \ref{fig:settlements-rank} [@Hayashi2007LongTerm; @OECD2024Africapolis]. Cross-checking city-proper and metropolitan entries confirms zero duplicate alias keys and clear separation between municipal and agglomeration series [@KNBS2019KenyaCensus; @UBOS2024UgandaCensus].

```{r fig3-ranksize, results='asis'}
viscount_figure(
  "figures/fig_03_rank_size.png",
  "Zipf rank-size curve across 1.764 deduplicated urban settlements (upper-tier q = 1,06, R² = 0,99) and top ten sub-regional densities in 2025AD.",
  "fig:settlements-rank",
  arg3_options = list(max_height = "0.38\\textheight")
)
```

# Results

## Country-Level Urban Ledger Summary

Table \ref{tab:country-summary-gazetteer} summarises settlement counts, city-proper versus metropolitan splits, observation totals and active interpolated counts at four benchmarks across all twelve countries in the gazetteer.

```{r tab-country-summary, results='asis'}
sum_rows <- lapply(all_country_order, function (cn) {
  sub <- entries_by_country[[cn]]
  c_disp <- if (identical(cn, "United Republic of Tanzania")) {
    "Tanzania"
  } else if (identical(cn, "Democratic Republic of the Congo")) {
    "DR Congo"
  } else {
    cn
  }
  n_cp <- sum(vapply(sub, function (e) !identical(e$population_scope, "metro"), logical(1)))
  n_me <- sum(vapply(sub, function (e) identical(e$population_scope, "metro"), logical(1)))
  n_obs <- sum(vapply(sub, function (e) length(e$population), integer(1)))
  act_61 <- sum(vapply(sub, function (e) !is.na(interp_site_pop(e, 1961)), logical(1)))
  act_00 <- sum(vapply(sub, function (e) !is.na(interp_site_pop(e, 2000)), logical(1)))
  act_25 <- sum(vapply(sub, function (e) !is.na(interp_site_pop(e, 2025)), logical(1)))
  top_nm <- if (length(sub) > 0L) paste0(sub[[1]]$name, " (", viscount_fmt_pop(entry_peak(sub[[1]])), ")") else "-"
  data.frame(
    Polity = c_disp,
    Sites = viscount_fmt_number(length(sub), 0L),
    City = viscount_fmt_number(n_cp, 0L),
    Metro = viscount_fmt_number(n_me, 0L),
    Obs = viscount_fmt_number(n_obs, 0L),
    `1961AD` = viscount_fmt_number(act_61, 0L),
    `2000AD` = viscount_fmt_number(act_00, 0L),
    `2025AD` = viscount_fmt_number(act_25, 0L),
    `Leading Entry` = top_nm,
    check.names = FALSE,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
})
tot_cp <- sum(vapply(all_entries, function (e) !identical(e$population_scope, "metro"), logical(1)))
tot_me <- sum(vapply(all_entries, function (e) identical(e$population_scope, "metro"), logical(1)))
tot_row <- data.frame(
  Polity = "All Countries",
  Sites = viscount_fmt_number(length(all_entries), 0L),
  City = viscount_fmt_number(tot_cp, 0L),
  Metro = viscount_fmt_number(tot_me, 0L),
  Obs = viscount_fmt_number(summary_cache$observation_count, 0L),
  `1961AD` = viscount_fmt_number(n_active[["1961"]], 0L),
  `2000AD` = viscount_fmt_number(n_active[["2000"]], 0L),
  `2025AD` = viscount_fmt_number(n_active[["2025"]], 0L),
  `Leading Entry` = "Kisumu / Nairobi (17,56M / 15,95M)",
  check.names = FALSE,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
df_csum <- rbind(do.call(rbind, sum_rows), tot_row)
rownames(df_csum) <- NULL
viscount_table(
  df_csum,
  "Country-level summary of assessed settlements, spatial scopes, dated observations and active counts at 1961AD, 2000AD and 2025AD.",
  arg3_options = list(label = "tab:country-summary-gazetteer")
)
```

Table \ref{tab:gaz-kenya} records all `r viscount_fmt_number(length(entries_by_country[["Kenya"]]), 0L)` assessed towns and agglomerations in Kenya (389 city-proper and 29 metropolitan entries), led by Nairobi (4,40M city-proper in 2019; 15,95M agglomeration in 2025AD), Mombasa (2,13M agglomeration), Nakuru (2,31M), Kisumu and Eldoret [@KNBS2019KenyaCensus; @Clark2013TransitionsAdulthood].

# Limitations

Three caveats govern this gazetteer. First, combining city-proper census series with Africapolis morphological agglomerations means summed column totals across Tables \ref{tab:gaz-kenya} to \ref{tab:gaz-border} overlap where metropolitan entries encompass nested constituent towns. Second, linear interpolation leaves hyphens (-) outside each settlement's earliest and latest observed dates, so 1961AD counts (157 entries) understate smaller district towns first enumerated after 1990AD. Third, 145 cross-border towns lie outside the five East African republics and are omitted from national admin-1 area totals in the companion review.

# Conclusion

Together, the `r viscount_fmt_number(length(all_entries), 0L)` entries in this gazetteer trace the post-colonial transformation of East Africa's urban network from 157 recorded towns in 1961AD to 1.240 active centres in 2025AD, documenting both statutory municipal growth and cross-border conurbation expansion across all twelve countries.

# Appendix

## Interpolated Urban Ledger Totals by Country

Table \ref{tab:appendix-gaz-totals} reports combined interpolated populations across each country's city-proper subset at six post-colonial benchmarks, avoiding double counting from metropolitan entries.

```{r tab-appendix-totals, results='asis'}
app_rows <- lapply(all_country_order, function (cn) {
  sub <- Filter(function (e) !identical(e$population_scope, "metro"), entries_by_country[[cn]])
  c_disp <- if (identical(cn, "United Republic of Tanzania")) {
    "Tanzania"
  } else if (identical(cn, "Democratic Republic of the Congo")) {
    "DR Congo"
  } else {
    cn
  }
  sums <- setNames(vapply(bench_nums, function (yr) {
    vals <- vapply(sub, function (e) {
      p <- interp_site_pop(e, yr)
      if (is.na(p) || p <= 0) 0 else p
    }, numeric(1))
    viscount_fmt_pop(sum(vals))
  }, character(1)), bench_keys)
  data.frame(
    `Polity (City-Proper)` = paste0(c_disp, " (", viscount_fmt_number(length(sub), 0L), ")"),
    `1961AD` = sums[["1961"]],
    `1976AD` = sums[["1976"]],
    `1991AD` = sums[["1991"]],
    `2000AD` = sums[["2000"]],
    `2015AD` = sums[["2015"]],
    `2025AD` = sums[["2025"]],
    check.names = FALSE,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
})
all_cp <- Filter(function (e) !identical(e$population_scope, "metro"), all_entries)
tot_sums <- setNames(vapply(bench_nums, function (yr) {
  vals <- vapply(all_cp, function (e) {
    p <- interp_site_pop(e, yr)
    if (is.na(p) || p <= 0) 0 else p
  }, numeric(1))
  viscount_fmt_pop(sum(vals))
}, character(1)), bench_keys)
tot_app <- data.frame(
  `Polity (City-Proper)` = paste0("All City-Proper (", viscount_fmt_number(length(all_cp), 0L), ")"),
  `1961AD` = tot_sums[["1961"]],
  `1976AD` = tot_sums[["1976"]],
  `1991AD` = tot_sums[["1991"]],
  `2000AD` = tot_sums[["2000"]],
  `2015AD` = tot_sums[["2015"]],
  `2025AD` = tot_sums[["2025"]],
  check.names = FALSE,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
df_app <- rbind(do.call(rbind, app_rows), tot_app)
rownames(df_app) <- NULL
viscount_table(
  df_app,
  "Combined interpolated populations across all 1.838 city-proper settlement entries by country from 1961AD to 2025AD.",
  arg3_options = list(label = "tab:appendix-gaz-totals")
)
```

# Footnotes

Linear interpolation is bounded strictly between each settlement's earliest and latest dated observation; periods outside an entry's observed span are marked with a hyphen (-). City-proper and metropolitan scopes are explicitly separated in Table \ref{tab:country-summary-gazetteer} and Table \ref{tab:appendix-gaz-totals} to prevent double counting of peri-urban suburbs.
